items.title: Derek Brown interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, March 5, 2021
items.q: I just finished a biography of Leonardo DaVinci.

ctx.x: I mean I definitely am, yeah. Because I have two little ones as we talked about, both under age two. And just the other day, walking him in his stroller and I was thinking what’s another kind of song, a different approach I could do to a live gig. And oh wow, we’re already at the park. So I know that happens. I think I have worked on the skill and I think you have to learn it, of also trying to be present in the rest of the world, like in my marriage and with my family. But I learned it the hard way in the sense…

don’t know what to do.” And then my dad saying, “Hey, maybe you need a day off.” I mean I had this conversation literally six months ago. This pandemic is bringing out a lot of issues I think, for us musicians. And it’s a lot of good stuff we need to deal with if we deal with it. And it was, “Maybe you need a day off. Have you ever taken a complete day off from the saxophone?” And it’s like, “No, that’s the number one thing I preach is practice every day.” And yes there’s different types of people. Some people…
Did you ever have the experience playing in combos where you found it dissatisfying. Did that have anything to do with you choosing to be mostly a solo artist?
